{{Short description|Mathematical group}}
{{For|the 3-dimensional Lie groups or Lie algebras|Bianchi classification}}

In [[mathematics]], a '''Bianchi group''' is a [[group (mathematics)|group]] of the form

:<math>\text{PSL}_2(\mathcal{O}_d)</math>

where ''d'' is a positive [[square-free integer]]. Here, <math>\text{PSL}_2</math> denotes the [[projective special linear group]] and <math>\mathcal{O}_d</math> is the [[ring of integers]] of the [[imaginary quadratic field]] <math>\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})</math>.

The groups were first studied by {{harvs|txt|last=Bianchi|authorlink=Luigi Bianchi|year=1892}} as a natural class of [[Discrete group|discrete subgroups]] of <math>\text{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})</math>, now termed [[Kleinian group]]s.

==Geometry==

As a subgroup of <math>\text{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})</math>, a Bianchi group acts by [[orientation-preserving]] [[isometry|isometries]] on three-dimensional [[hyperbolic space]] <math>\mathbb{H}^3</math>. The quotient

:<math>M_d=\text{PSL}_2(\mathcal{O}_d)\backslash\mathbb{H}^3</math>

is a non-compact, hyperbolic 3-fold of finite volume, called a '''Bianchi orbifold'''. An exact formula for its volume in terms of the [[Dedekind zeta function]] of the underlying imaginary quadratic field was computed by [[Marie Georges Humbert|Humbert]]. If <math>D</math> is the discriminant of <math>\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})</math>, then

:<math>\operatorname{vol}(M_d)=\frac{|D|^{3/2}}{4\pi^2}\zeta_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})}(2).</math>

The cusps of <math>M_d</math> are in bijection with the ideal classes of <math>\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-d})</math>. Consequently, the number of cusps is equal to the [[class number]] of the field.

==Arithmetic properties==

Bianchi groups are [[arithmetic group|arithmetic]] Kleinian groups. Every non-cocompact arithmetic Kleinian group is commensurable, up to conjugacy in <math>\text{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})</math>, with a Bianchi group.<ref name=MR58>Maclachlan & Reid (2003) p. 58</ref>
